Abstract:
Stress has emerged as a critical concern affecting cognitive performance, productivity, and overall well-being in modern academic and professional environments. Existing stress detection systems predominantly rely on invasive wearable physiological sensors or single-modality approaches, limiting their practical applicability and real-time usability. This work addresses these limitations by presenting a non-invasive, multimodal stress detection system that integrates facial expression analysis, eye-blink rate monitoring, and speech emotion analysis. The system utilizes a laptop's built-in camera and microphone to continuously capture behavioral cues without requiring external hardware. Each modality is processed through dedicated machine learning models-DenseNet-161 for facial emotions (fine-tuned on FER2013 and AffectNet datasets), MediaPipe Face Mesh with Eye Aspect Ratio computation for blink analysis, and Xception for speech emotion analysis (fine-tuned on RAVDESS dataset). A majority voting algorithm combines predictions from all three modalities to determine the final stress classification. The system operates entirely on-device, ensuring privacy and enabling real-time monitoring over extended durations. Experimental validation with 52 participants demonstrated 90.38% user-reported accuracy, confirming the system's effectiveness in real-world scenarios. This multimodal approach provides a practical, accessible solution for continuous stress monitoring in everyday environments, with potential applications in workplace wellness, mental health monitoring, and educational settings.
